evidenceRules: Timestamps are positions in the supplied recordings, not claims about original gameplay duration.
Visible 2x playback markers prohibit movement-speed, animation-timing, countdown-rate or transition-duration acceptance without correction.
Player-authored nameplates are excluded from required product copy.
No audio, hidden scoring formula, backend hierarchy, remote name or server calculation is inferred from the footage.

observed: The avatar moves from a bright school common area into the red/white gym and approaches the court while the compact roam HUD remains visible.
No entry prompt or hidden trigger is visible in this sampled span.
Active play replaces the roam presentation with a top team-style score strip and central circular count, plus bottom personal points, heart-like indicators and a ball-count icon.
Thrown balls and other players are visible on the court.
Transient point increments and a knockout message appear during play.
A notebook overlay displays Finish!, followed by a team-winner message.
A Report Card follows with activity title, grade, personal score, KOs, hits and a per-player result table.
After the result closes, coin-style +45 feedback appears in the gym.
The avatar is back in the school common area with the compact roam HUD and can move and open inventory.
A level toast is visible but its cause is not proven by the class sequence.
A Science activity Report Card is open in a classroom.
After it closes, coin-style +45 feedback appears at a classroom workstation.
The avatar leaves the workstation/classroom and resumes corridor free roam with item slots and the right icon rail.
The avatar is first shown in outdoor free roam with a compact schedule strip.
A black crest transition is followed by arrival in a bright wood-floor activity room.
A notebook instruction overlay appears before active play.
Active play uses four vertical lanes, directional notes, Q/W/E/R prompts, a horizontal progress line, visible streak/multiplier/score fields and transient point feedback.
The room and other avatars remain visible behind the activity overlay.
A Report Card replaces the active overlay and includes the activity title, grade, score, accuracy and a per-player result table.
After the report closes, coin-style +41 feedback appears and the avatar resumes movement in the activity room.
A second activity room presents notebook instructions, active task-specific UI and another Report Card, supporting the same broad instruction-active-result structure.
The clip ends before a full free-roam return from this second activity is shown.
Room/world entry precedes activity instructions or active play.
Activity-specific HUD is distinct from the compact roam HUD.
In-play feedback changes while the activity remains active.
Completion can include Finish!, winner feedback and a Report Card.
Coin-style reward feedback appears after the result closes.
The player can resume movement after completion.

canonicalAuthorityAudit.scheduleEvidence: default.project.json maps FoundationBootstrap; it writes SchoolDay/SchoolPeriod* attributes and emits period/session events.
canonicalAuthorityAudit.classSessionAuthority: school/src/server/ClassSessionController.lua owns only per-player ephemeral activity state and must not advance the school day or period.
canonicalAuthorityAudit.dormantDuplicateSource: school/src/server/SchoolLoop.server.lua contains a separate period loop but is not mapped by default.project.json at input SHA; it must remain unmapped or be removed in a separately authorized cleanup.
canonicalAuthorityAudit.currentPresentationGap: CanonicalSchoolClient renders ClassActivityCatalog multiple-choice prompts and choices in one modal; it does not implement the observed room-based dodgeball or lane-rhythm activity presentations.
canonicalAuthorityAudit.priorityConstraint: Do not expand custom curriculum before reference gameplay baseline.

observableStateContract.acceptance: Compact roam HUD and schedule context are visible; no activity overlay owns the screen.
A bounded transition into the assigned room occurs without creating another school clock or schedule writer; exact trigger and duration remain implementation choices until separately observed.
When instructions exist, a dismissible notebook-style card names the activity and explains controls without exposing hidden answer/scoring authority.

Activity-specific controls, shared progress/score context and personal feedback update during play; the server validates outcomes and the client cannot authoritatively write score, completion or reward.
Input closes once, completion feedback is visible, and late/replayed input cannot create a second completion.
A report-style result summarizes the observed metrics appropriate to the activity without claiming formulas not established by footage.
Any reward is emitted once through the existing progression/economy authority; the class lane does not create a second ledger.
The activity overlay clears and control returns to roam or the next scheduled activity; period/session exit clears ephemeral state exactly once.

producerAcceptanceCriteria: Implement only after Control Tower authorizes one exact-base producer for the class/activity slice.
Preserve FoundationBootstrap as the only mapped day/period/schedule authority.
Preserve ClassSessionController as the only active per-player class/activity session authority; activity implementations plug into it rather than creating parallel session loops.
Add no custom schoolwork/curriculum content in this parity slice.

Model dodgeball and lane-rhythm as activity-specific presentation/interaction adapters with server-validated completion and replay-safe results; do not encode unobserved exact scoring formulas as reference truth.
Completion orders finish/winner feedback, report card, single reward feedback and return/advance state as supported by the relevant clip.
The compact roam HUD is restored after the activity presentation clears.
No new clock, progression, persistence or economy writer is introduced.
qaAcceptanceCriteria: Static tests cover legal state ordering, single completion, replay/late-input rejection, period-change exit and reward handoff without validating guessed score formulas.
Rendered comparison binds to the exact candidate SHA at A@01:00-02:08 and B@00:00-00:12/01:00-01:21.
Functional, visual, interaction and target-device evidence statuses remain separate.
Static CI cannot certify appearance, feel, input timing or mobile obstruction.
Any timing comparison corrects for visible 2x playback or remains NOT_EVALUATED.
